They should feel bleak. I'm in a Conservative stronghold. It has returned a conservative almost every election since it was created. It will likely go conservative again.. ..but maybe not. Looking forward to Monday. This will be interesting.

There is no doubt that Stephen Harper and the Conservative Party are going to come out of this election with less power/seats than when they went in, even they have admitted that another Conservative majority government is unlikely, and I am interested in what will happen to Harper come Tuesday.

Unless they end up with at least a minority I believe that Harper will leave immediately, if it is a minority and if Trudeau & Mulcair stick to their promises not to support a Harper minority the party will also force Harper to leave, and if Harper and the CPC end up in 2nd or 3rd place Harper is likely to step down as leader Monday evening, and as MP very shortly thereafter - he's not interested in being a "useful bench warmer" (his words not mine) for the new party leader.

I cannot help but think that when he is sitting alone in a dim campaign plane at night Harper is kicking himself in the ass for not leaving before this election was called, I see in his decision to try and hold on to the big chair one more time the same arrogance I saw in Paul Martin just before his minority government fell in November of 2005. I don't see Harper coming out of this election any better than Martin, and I certainly don't see him being remembered with anywhere near the fondness [maybe even limited respect?] Paul Martin still commands.
